$comment: Every finding from every audit, with a status. verify-all.ps1 fails while any entry is 'open'. This file exists because one finding - the allow-before-deny bug in hooks/subagent-rules.cjs - was found by an audit, reported, and then never re-read by four later audits, so it shipped for two days. An audit that reports into a chat log cannot remember; an audit that reports into a file that gates the build cannot forget.

rules.open: the audit fails. Fix it, or change the status with a reason.
rules.fixed: must carry 'evidence' - the commit or the command that proves it. verify-all checks that the cited commit exists.
rules.wontfix: must carry 'reason'. A defect accepted on purpose, with the reason someone can disagree with later.
rules.verified_by: the audit round that found it, so a re-read is possible.

findings.title: subagent-rules.cjs evaluates the allow list before the deny list, and both use bidirectional prefix fuzz, so an agent named <allowed>-anything is treated as trusted
findings.note: Latent today (0 collisions among 3 allow / 14 deny names). Exploitable the moment an agent file named like an allowed one is installed. The safe shape is exact match for allow, fuzz only for deny.

findings.title: docs/reference/skills.md line 25 is a 4-cell row in a 3-column table
findings.note: Commit 1f3f7bd claimed to fix this and changed only the cell text. The row is still malformed. Measured: cols=4 against a header of cols=3.

findings.title: Three file reads in verify-all.ps1 are unguarded, so a failed read can leave the previous iteration's value in the variable
findings.note: The same class was fixed at six other sites. These three were not found because the fix was applied where it was noticed rather than searched for.

findings.title: verify-all.ps1 had no exit statement, so every finding printed and the exit code was always 0
workspace-sync.ps1 -Write deleted the whole memory mirror when -RepoMemory was omitted
sap-auth-probe.js built an https request for an http URL, threw at module scope, and exited 1 - which the contract defines as STALE
Secret-Present returned a boolean or the string 'ERROR', and PowerShell coerces the right operand of -eq, so a healthy secret compared equal to 'ERROR'
Parked skills were silently reinstalled by the toolkit upgrade, costing 805 tokens per request, with no check able to see it
subagent-rules.cjs matched only file stems while the harness sends the frontmatter display name, so every allowlisted agent was classified 'not listed in roster.json' and restricted
findings.note: Proved from this machine's own hook log, which recorded 'restricted SAP ABAP Reverse Engineering Analyst by Pongg' on the day the agent was allowed. The roster now carries display/displays, and the hook also matches the display name without its ' by <author>' suffix.

findings.title: session-drift.cjs called serverNamesCli(), which reads MCP_CLI_JSON - a constant that was never declared - so every run threw and no snapshot was written
findings.note: Introduced by the fix for F-012 and caught by QA, not by the audit: section 1b only runs node --check, and a missing identifier parses cleanly. The hook's own header calls a silent no-op the worst failure mode.

findings.title: verify-all.ps1 section 1b counted every Node file as parsed even when node was absent from PATH
findings.note: Reproduced by trimming PATH: the same '332 verified' printed with node invisible. Now prints SKIP and excludes the files from Ran.

findings.title: verify-all.ps1 section 1 accepted any later '---' as a frontmatter fence, so a file whose frontmatter an edit had destroyed still passed
verify-all.ps1 declared a -Summary switch and then overwrote it, so -Detail full -Summary printed the full output the caller had asked to suppress
Ran 'parked', Ran 'toolkit' and Ran 'mcp-sources' were registered for sections that examined nothing, which made a clean run unreachable (exit 2) on machines without those inputs
findings.note: The same defect was fixed for two counters and reintroduced for a third in the same commit, which is why the fix is now a stated rule next to each call site rather than a local patch.

findings.title: verify-all.ps1 discarded git grep's exit code, so a failed history scan printed 'history clean across N commit(s)'
install-kit.ps1 never installed hooks/*.cjs, and its byte comparison could never report a difference, so it was not idempotent either
findings.note: Measured cause of a live subagent-rules.cjs that was a full version behind the clone. Nine tracked files were CRLF in the working tree despite eol=lf, which is what kept the 'line-ending only' counter at five forever.

findings.title: sap-connection.ps1 derived PRESENT/ABSENT from the helper's exit code, so a helper that crashed was reported as 'no password stored'
findings.note: An uncaught terminating error in a -File script exits 1, which is also what a deliberate 'nothing stored' exit looks like. The verdict now comes from the output token.

findings.title: lesson-capture.cjs treated any occurrence of 'aborted' as a user cancel, discarding real network failures
measure-context.ps1, who-locks.ps1 and workspace-sync.ps1 reported a pass for input they had not examined
findings.note: A missing skill root printed 'skills 0 files' and exit 0; an unreadable pid printed nothing; a -Check without -RepoMemory said 'mirror matches the source' for a folder it never read.

findings.title: Three MCP servers are declared in both %APPDATA%\Code\User\mcp.json and ~/.copilot/mcp-config.json, and VS Code imports the second by default and disables one copy of each duplicate
findings.verified_by: measured 2026-11-15 from the shipped VS Code 1.146 bundle
findings.note: Pyo sets copilot discovery on by default and chat.mcp.collisionBehavior defaults to 'disable'. Fixed by setting chat.mcp.discovery.enabled.copilot=false, and gated by verify-all section 8b, which fails while duplicates remain and the source is on.

findings.title: The agent's ownership gate forbade and permitted the same act eleven lines apart, and claimed only one skill was editable while the kit ships five
The routing tie-break told the agent to 'attempt the call' to test ARC-1 callability, which authorised a SAP call before the pre-flight target gate
findings.note: The sentence was a verbatim copy of docs/tool-routing.md, which is how the same rule came to mean two different things in two homes.

findings.title: Four documentation statements were false: a skill costs nothing until used, all MCP servers live in mcp.json, a non-existent ~/.copilot/mcp.json, and a lock-recount command that printed 83 lines instead of one number
Nine tracked files were CRLF in the working tree although .gitattributes pins eol=lf
findings.note: Invisible to git, visible to install-kit's byte comparison. Renormalised; a fresh install now converges at 22 identical on the second run.

findings.title: The SE38 and reverse-engineering agents declare read-only default-deny in prose but have no tools: list, so the harness grants them every tool
findings.reason: A tools: list cannot express 'read-only SAP': 'arc-1/*' is one entry covering SAPWrite and SAPActivate as well, which is how the other read-only agent (ST22) is configured already. Narrowing the list without narrowing ARC-1 would move the restriction from prose to nothing, and a list that omits a tool the agent needs fails mid-task. The real control is ARC-1's own SAP_ALLOW_WRITES and SAP_ALLOWED_PACKAGES, plus the prose gate.

findings.title: verify-all.ps1 never reads %APPDATA%\Code\User\settings.json, which holds a plaintext ADT MCP token
findings.reason: The token is a field of the SAPSE.adt-vscode extension (adt.mcpServer.token), which offers no ${input:...} or credential-store indirection, so no rewrite removes it. The file lives outside every repository and is never tracked, and the token value is already covered in tracked files by the local pattern list. Adding settings.json to the literal-secret scan would fail every run for a value that has no supported alternative, which is the false-positive class this audit is trying to eliminate.

findings.notes: Measured 44.8 ms per process, vs 50 ms total for one git cat-file --batch-check fed all refs on stdin. A/B over 4 alternating runs: 3,449 -> 2,344 ms (-32%). The batch form also reports the object type, so evidence resolving to a blob or tree is now rejected instead of accepted for existing.
findings.title: Section 10 spawned one git process per evidence ref: 23 refs cost 1,030 ms of a 3,400 ms audit

findings.notes: (git rev-parse HEAD) -eq (git rev-parse origin/main) compares null with null, and $null -eq $null is True; @(git status --porcelain).Count is 0 when the command failed. Both now read the exit code first. Demonstrated against a directory with no .git: rev-parse rc=128, previously reported as the good state.
findings.title: Section 7 printed synced=True and dirty=0 when git itself failed

findings.notes: Those scripts inherit Continue, the mode that lets a read fail silently. who-locks.ps1 was outside the gate while the summary claimed to cover M continue-on-error scripts. Population is now every script that has not opted into Stop: 2 -> 3 scripts, 30 reads. Negative-tested with a synthetic script holding an unguarded ReadAllText and no EAP line.
findings.title: Section 1c selected its population by looking for a literal EAP=Continue declaration, excluding every script that never mentions the variable

findings.notes: The JSON-shape regex needs "KEY": and section 9 needs a quote after =, so the identical secret scored 1 as an object and 0 in both sections as an argument pair, with the run printing OK and exiting 0. A second regex now covers KEY=VALUE and skips indirections; both regexes are self-tested on four synthetic inputs before use.
findings.where: tooling/verify-all.ps1 section 8 and the shape regex in section 9
findings.title: Section 8 could not see a secret passed as --env KEY=VALUE, the form its own header cites as the reason it exists; section 9 could not see it either

findings.notes: In a double-quoted string ${input:...} is a variable and expanded to empty; in a single-quoted string passed to -f, {input:...} is a format placeholder and -f throws, which under EAP=Continue is statement-terminating. Both were introduced and caught in the same session. The section now counts one verdict per config and reports an ISSUE if any config produced none, so a swallowed finding cannot pass silently again.
findings.title: Two versions of section 8 reporting line swallowed the finding it had just detected

findings.notes: The other two roots were guarded and warned; the memory folder was not, so a redirected APPDATA gave memory 0 files, a smaller TOTAL and exit 0 with no warning. Measured 31,625 -> 25,574 chars and zero warnings before the fix.
findings.title: measure-context printed a healthy zero when the memory folder did not exist

findings.notes: path.join(process.env.APPDATA || , ...) yields Code\\User\\mcp.json; the read fails, the snapshot stores an empty list, and the next session reports all five servers as newly added. lesson-capture.cjs already had the homedir fallback.
findings.title: session-drift built a relative mcp.json path when APPDATA was unset, then recorded zero servers as fact

findings.notes: if (prev) treats a truncated snapshot as a first run, so drift detection is silently off for that session and the truncated file is then overwritten. The snapshot is now written to a temporary file and renamed, and an unreadable previous snapshot produces an explicit line instead of silence.
findings.title: session-drift could not distinguish a first run from an unreadable snapshot, and its non-atomic write destroyed the evidence

findings.notes: keys() reads entry.files and entry.displays and the deny list is built with them, so a delegatable entry written in the sibling shape was classified not listed and its agent was restricted. Demonstrated: old code restricted a files:[...] entry, new code trusts it, and a look-alike name is still restricted.
findings.title: subagent-rules projected the allow list to {file, display, role}, dropping the files/displays spellings its own keys() supports

findings.notes: 0.84 MB after 10,000 events, growing for the life of the machine. Capped at 64 KB by keeping the newest 250 lines when the cap is crossed. session-drift already rotated its snapshot; this hook had no equivalent.
findings.title: subagent-rules appended to its log forever: 88 bytes per subagent start, no cap, rotation or truncation path

findings.notes: The directory loop runs before the per-file -Check tests. Demonstrated with a clean fake home: -Check created agents/, hooks/, skills/ and state/. Now guarded, and the same test creates zero directories.
findings.title: install-kit -Check promised to copy nothing but created all four destination directories

findings.notes: The installer tooling filter takes every .ps1/.js/.json except surface.json, so the ledger became a live file no section compared; measured live 14,721 bytes against 17,834 in the clone with no DRIFT line, and -Force would have replaced the live one silently. findings.json is now in the pair list.
findings.title: install-kit copies tooling\\findings.json into the live state folder, but section 7 never compared it

findings.notes: Secret-State in the same script correctly reports UNKNOWN for the same failure. Demonstrated with a nonexistent helper: old code claimed success and exited 0; new code warns and prints the command that would remove it.
findings.title: sap-connection -Remove -AlsoSecret printed that the stored secret was removed without checking the helper exit code

findings.notes: Zero rows was indistinguishable from a completed check that found no holder. It now says which case happened: no such process, no matching directory, or no candidate process.
findings.title: who-locks printed nothing and exited 0 for a nonexistent -Pid or a -Match that matched nothing

findings.notes: 67,477 bytes under Microsoft\\Windows\\PowerShell\\, created when a child powershell.exe ran with LOCALAPPDATA unset or redirected, which is what a sandboxed parent does. Microsoft/ and **/ModuleAnalysisCache are ignored and the folder was deleted; verified that the ignore rule hides a recreated copy.
findings.title: PowerShell ModuleAnalysisCache appeared inside the repository, untracked and not ignored

findings.notes: Evidence: ~/.copilot/state/subagent-rules.log gained five entries during one session. The blanket claim came from one event (surface.json takenAt unchanged after a reload) and was generalised. Replaced with a dated per-event table: subagentStart fires, sessionStart writes the snapshot but the event name is unverified, postToolUseFailure has produced no ledger. The surviving rule is that no hook is reported as having run without a log line or a changed file.
findings.where: docs/reference/environment.md, docs/architecture.md, README.md, skills/mcp-surface-audit, skills/capture-lesson, user memory memory-setup.md
findings.title: Six places stated that hooks never fire in the Copilot harness; subagentStart is observed firing

findings.reason: Demonstrated: killing only the launcher powershell leaves the npx cmd.exe and its node child alive 2.5 s later, because the grandchild inherits the client pipe and never sees EOF. Fixing it needs a Job Object with JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE, which means P/Invoke plus control of the child creation instead of & $exe @rest - and a mistake there breaks the JSON-RPC stdio channel, which is a worse failure than an orphan. The harness normally kills the whole tree, and the cost is one idle node process per abandoned session.
findings.title: The launcher leaves an orphaned cmd.exe and node.exe behind when only the launcher process is killed

findings.reason: Measured: one node process using vm.Script for all four files takes 47 ms against 200 ms, saving 153 ms. vm.Script does not accept ESM syntax that node --check accepts for .mjs and ESM .js, so a future file would be reported as broken while it runs. A false positive in the parse gate is worse than 153 ms, which is why the batched form was measured and rejected rather than adopted.
findings.title: Section 1b spends about 200 ms on four node --check processes, and the obvious speedup carries a false-positive risk

findings.reason: Measured 125 bytes per row and a full read plus rewrite at lines 141 and 157: about 6.2 GB cumulative after 10,000 events (ESTIMATE from the per-row measurement). Per-event wall time is still nearly flat at this size (88 ms at one row, 91 ms at 8,000), so the cost is not yet real. Switching to append-only would mean the row format has to survive partial writes, which is a design change to the lesson ledger rather than a fix. Bounded since 2026-11-16 by the 256 KB cap added in F-056: the quadratic term stops at roughly 4,000 rows. The per-event whole-file rewrite remains, and remains accepted.
findings.title: lesson-capture rewrites the whole ledger for every event, so cumulative I/O grows with the square of the row count
Read-Utf8 promised a sentinel string in its own comment and returned an empty string, so an unreadable memory or SKILL file was summed as a zero-char file and the TOTAL shrank with no warning
findings.note: The comment said "returning a sentinel string makes the failure visible"; the code returned ''. Every call site summed it. Measured 2026-11-16 with memory-setup.md held open FileShare.None: before the fix the tool printed a smaller TOTAL and exit 0; after it prints "WARNING 1 file(s) unreadable, their chars are NOT in this total: memory/memory-setup.md".

findings.title: A trailing newline was counted as a line, so the 200-line memory budget reported 102 lines for 99 and could fail a compliant tree at the boundary
findings.note: Measured on the live memory folder: split=21/56/25 against real 20/55/24. The budget is a gate, so at 198 real lines it printed "exceeds the 200-line budget by 1" and exited 1. workspace-sync.ps1 already contained the correct definition in Get-LineCount, so the repository held the right rule in one file and the wrong one in two.

findings.title: Every CredRead failure was reported as ABSENT, so a logon-session or ACL failure told the user to re-enter a password that was already stored
findings.note: GetLastWin32Error was discarded. ERROR_NOT_FOUND is 1168; 1312 (no such logon session) and 5 (access denied) are not the same fact. -Test now prints ABSENT only for 1168 and UNKNOWN plus the Win32 error otherwise; sap-connection.ps1 already maps anything that is neither PRESENT nor ABSENT to ERROR, so no caller changed.

findings.title: A failed ledger read was treated as "no ledger", and the next line overwrote the real ledger with a header plus one row
findings.note: catch set existing='', then "if (!existing.trim()) existing = HEADER", then writeFileSync. One sharing violation destroyed every captured failure and reset the occurrence counter that is the hook's only output. Only ENOENT now means "no ledger yet". Measured: with the file held FileShare.None the hook printed "cannot read ... (EBUSY); ledger not touched" and the 5-line ledger stayed at 5 lines; unlocked it appended to 6.

findings.title: -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue made an unscannable file look clean in the one gate that exists to stop a password reaching a repository
findings.note: The override beat the script's top-level Stop, the enumeration yielded nothing, and an empty set is exactly what a clean file produces. An unreadable file is now a refusal, the rule verify-all section 9 already applies to itself. Measured: with a contract file held FileShare.None the script printed "refusing to mirror - cannot scan for credentials" and exited 1; unlocked it printed the plan and exited 0.

findings.title: The evidence check compared git cat-file's raw output line to 'commit', so the 'no such object' branch could never fire and a missing commit was misdiagnosed
findings.note: Proved 2026-11-16: "deadbeef..." through git cat-file --batch-check="%(objecttype)" prints "deadbeef... missing" and exits 0, so the whole line was compared and the diagnostic read "resolves to a deadbeef... missing, not a commit". Get-EvidenceType now strips the missing marker, and a four-case self-test runs on every audit.

findings.title: The audit and the drift hook read only .file on the allow side while the roster's own comment and the hook allow files:[...], so a valid roster produced a false GONE and a false exit 1
findings.note: The other half of F-035: the hook was taught both spellings, the three readers that feed the gate were not. Measured by adding "files": ["zz-symmetry-probe"] to a live roster entry: before, known stayed 17 and nothing was reported; after, known=18 GONE=1 and two more probe cases. Roster restored byte-identical.

findings.title: The derived short display name sat on the ALLOW list, so an agent installed as <display minus " by X"> was trusted although the roster never named it
findings.note: For this roster the three keys were sap-se38-report-tester, sap-st22-dump-analyst and sap-abap-reverse-engineering-analyst, none of which equals a file stem. Section 5c could not see it because it probed only .file. The spelling is still used, but on the deny side, where a wider match is the safe direction; section 5c now probes it and expects RESTRICTED. Proved by the audit failing with three ISSUEs against the installed hook before it was reinstalled, and passing after.

findings.title: Two copies of the kit-root pin read ran unguarded under ErrorActionPreference Stop, so an unreadable pin killed the script instead of falling through to the next resolution step
findings.note: verify-all.ps1:46-48 is the fixed form and documents the trap; the other two copies did not. Measured: with kit-root.txt held FileShare.None, install-kit -Check now reports the source and exits 0 through the parent-folder fallback.

findings.title: A killed audit left its hookprobe-* home in TEMP for ever, because the cleanup lives only in a finally that a hard kill never reaches
findings.note: Measured 2026-11-16: hookprobe-15060 from the previous night was still present with two files. One directory and about 5.5 KB per killed run. Section 5c now sweeps homes older than an hour at start, which cannot touch a concurrent run.

findings.title: The lesson ledger had no cap, so it grew without limit and every failure rewrote the whole file
findings.note: Measured +71 bytes per event, about 750 KB at 10,000 failures, and the whole file was re-read and rewritten each time. Capped at 256 KB keeping the header and the newest 250 rows, the cap subagent-rules.cjs already uses. The quadratic rewrite itself is F-045 and stays accepted.

findings.title: Caching the 11 subagent-gate probes would save about 465 ms, and a cached security gate can report a verdict it did not compute
findings.reason: Measured: 470 ms for 11 node spawns at 42.7 ms each, 85% process startup. A content-hash cache would still be a green result nobody recomputed, which is the defect class this repository has spent four rounds removing. Running the probes concurrently needs 11 redirected stdio pairs and can deadlock; the audit is not on a hot path, so the coverage stays and the milliseconds go.

findings.title: Sections 1b and 1c both parse the same PowerShell files, and 9a scans every tracked file twice
findings.reason: Measured: 1b is 226 ms of which 148 ms is four node --check processes, and 1c parses only the 3 files that can lie, not all 8, so sharing the AST saves about 30 ms. 9a's two passes keep HIT and SHAPE apart on purpose and run under -ErrorAction Stop inside a try; merging them risks the split for 50 ms. Neither repays the coupling.

findings.title: The skill restated CDS and RAP design rules that sap-abap-cds and rap-development also state, so two copies could drift
findings.note: Not a file in this repository, so no commit can prove it. Done 2026-11-16: the CDS/RAP checkpoints (2,792 chars) and the per-program-type checklist (804 chars) moved verbatim into references\cds-rap-design-checkpoints.md and references\requirement-checks-by-program-type.md, each with a deferral sentence at the point of use. SKILL.md 14,855 -> 12,338 chars. Section 2 of verify-all now fails on a references/ link that does not resolve.
findings.evidence: live change 2026-11-16, file outside this repository

findings.title: Four kit skill descriptions could lose 191 chars, and two toolkit skills carry an identical 307-char clause
findings.reason: Measured: new-program 542 -> 437, capture-lesson 495 -> 437, rap-lifecycle 392 -> 369, long-task-control 315 -> 310, total 191 chars or about 48 tokens per request. The risk is skill selection, which depends on those words, and 48 tokens does not buy it. The abap-debugging / abap-runtime-analysis pair is worth about 419 chars but both are hash-tracked by the SAP toolkit, so any edit is reverted by the next upgrade and reported as EDITED by section 5b; the fix is a decision about which one wins, not an edit.

findings.title: The audit is about 100 ms slower than before, because section 5c now probes 14 shapes instead of 11
findings.reason: Measured A/B, four alternating runs of HEAD and the working tree: old 2,526 ms, new 2,625 ms. Three derived-name probes at 42.7 ms each plus the TEMP sweep. Accepted: the three probes are the only thing that would notice F-053 coming back, and 0.1 s on a manual audit buys nothing.

findings.title: The recovery snapshot could silently reinstate a rule that had been disproved, and nothing recorded which of its lines are not literal copies of the live machine
findings.note: The snapshot committed on 2026-11-15 still said hooks do not fire in this harness (disproved the same day), carried the pre-verify-all way of counting the 200-line budget, and pointed tool-surface matching at an agent comment block instead of the skill. README.md said only "check first" before Copy-Item *.md -Force, and it did not say that arc-1-mcp.md is stored sanitised. Measured 2026-11-16: memory-setup.md was 208 chars behind live and differed on all four points; arc-1-mcp.md differs on exactly 1 of 20 lines, the real NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS path, which contains a customer name. A restore is silent on success, so the false rule would have come back with no signal.

findings.title: The setup guide never installs roster.json or hooks.json, so following it leaves the audit unpassable and the subagent roster gate silently inert
findings.note: install-kit.ps1:189 and :195 print both as manual; the word roster appeared nowhere in the guide and hooks.json appears nowhere at all. Two consequences on a fresh machine: verify-all.ps1:501 reports ISSUE roster not found and exits 1, and three .cjs files sit in ~/.copilot/hooks with no event registered, so the security control that restricts un-rostered subagents never runs while section 10 tells the operator to confirm it is reporting. Section 3b now copies both, resolves {{COPILOT_HOME}} with a measured one-liner, and says node must be on PATH.

findings.where: SETUP-NEW-MACHINE.md section 7 vs section 10, tooling/verify-all.ps1 section 5b
findings.title: The guide told the operator to delete a toolkit skill after every reinstall and also required the audit to exit 0 - the two were mutually exclusive, on every machine, for ever
findings.note: Section 5b had a parked-file exception but no deleted-file one, so a documented deletion reported MISSING and exited 1. Measured before the fix: "MISSING skills\advanced-event-mesh-lifecycle\SKILL.md" and RESULT 1 problem. tooling/removed-on-purpose.json now declares nine removals with their reasons; 5b honours them and reports a declared skill that reappears as an ISSUE carrying the reason. Negative-tested both directions: a fake lean-build in ~/.agents/skills produced "declared deleted but installed again" plus the measured 67-char cost, and a fake live advanced-event-mesh-lifecycle produced the 5b revival line. Both removed afterwards.

findings.title: The routing reference still carried the sentence F-022 removed from the agent, so the tie-break still authorised a SAP call before the target gate
findings.note: F-022s own note says the sentence was a verbatim copy of docs/tool-routing.md and that this is how one rule came to mean two things in two homes - but only the agent copy was edited. The document now matches the fixed agent: observe callability only after the target is confirmed, with a call that reads no data.

findings.title: Three skills deleted on purpose were still named as loadable in the agent and in the skill, so an agent following either would issue a load that cannot resolve
findings.note: surgical-patch, safe-refactor and tdd. Nothing noticed because a skill name in prose is only text, and the instruction fails at the moment it is followed. Both now name ponytail, which is installed; the deleted names were removed entirely rather than annotated, so nothing can be read as an instruction. New gate section 3b checks every load/use/skill mention in the nine repository-owned files: measured 10 names, all resolving.

findings.title: The guide said 19 ABAP skills have no npx source and must be copied from a backup; 12 of them are lock-tracked to arc-mcp/arc-1
findings.note: Measured against ~/.agents/.skill-lock.json: exactly 7 are absent from the lock (senior-abap-development, sap-abap, sap-abap-cds, sapui5, sap-abap-reverse-engineering, sap-se38-report-tester, sap-st22-dump-analysis) and 12 resolve to arc-mcp/arc-1. docs/reference/skills.md:43-45 lists exactly those 7, and docs/reference/arc-1.md:23 has the command the guide omitted. A hand-copied skill is invisible to npx skills update, so the old text permanently froze 12 skills at their backup version.

findings.title: The history scan wrote its derived credential patterns to a temp file with cleanup only in a finally, so every hard-killed run left the identifiers themselves on disk
findings.note: The patterns are built from the ARC-1 connection store, so the leftover file is a file of customer identifiers. Measured 2026-11-16: verify-rx-5020.txt, 126 bytes, six pattern lines, left by a Ctrl+C. Proved that this git accepts -f - from stdin (rc 0 on a match, 1 on no match) and piped the patterns in, so no file is created. Removed the leftover; 0 remain.

findings.title: The hookprobe sweep decided by age alone, and a directory timestamp does not advance when a file is written into a subdirectory - so it could delete a live run home and turn a clean tree into a false exit 1
findings.note: Measured: with sub/x.txt created, the parent LastWriteTime was unchanged (03:09:05.707 before and after); with y.txt at the root it advanced. The hook writes its log into the .copilot subdirectory, so a run alive for over an hour kept a stale timestamp. The victim is hookprobe-<pid>, so the sweep now skips any directory whose PID is still alive.

findings.title: The log was truncated by a fixed 250 lines under a 64 KB byte cap, which cannot converge when a restricted line carries the roster whole reason
findings.note: Measured live log: 51 lines, mean 197 bytes, max 637, so 250 lines is up to 159 KB - above the cap, meaning every later event would re-read and re-write the whole file for ever. Truncation is now by bytes, keeping the last half-cap so the rewrite happens once per ~32 KB of events. Proved with a synthetic 137,600-byte log: the old rule would have left 137,600 bytes, the new one wrote 32,416 with the newest line intact.

findings.title: Seven command-level errors that would each stop or mislead an operator on a fresh machine
findings.note: All measured against the repository this session: (a) two of the four config templates are named mcp.json and settings.json but the files are mcp.json.template and settings.json.template; (b) the probe was invoked as .\tooling\sap-auth-probe.js, and .JS is in PATHEXT so Windows hands it to WScript, which has no require - it needs node, and it exits 2 UNKNOWN without ARC1_PROBE_URL/USER/PASS; (c) no execution-policy step, while a default Windows client is Restricted and blocks both .\x.ps1 and powershell -File x.ps1; (d) three of the eight delete targets come from mattpocock/skills, which the guide never installs, so they error on a clean machine; (e) the park step was described but never instructed, so section 0 18 skills was unreachable after a fresh toolkit install puts 24 live; (f) section 0 listed kit skills under ~/.agents/skills while install-kit.ps1 writes them to ~/.copilot/skills; (g) see 2 (no version) and 6 (group-3 skills see 7, a section with no such list).

findings.title: The reference-link gate checked only markdown links, so it validated 3 of 79 references
findings.note: Measured across the three loader roots: 3 markdown links and 76 backticked paths, all 76 resolving. The gate now checks both spellings, de-duplicated per file. Negative-tested with a scratch skill whose SKILL.md says Read `references/never-written.md`: reported BAD (broken reference), then clean after removal.

findings.title: The tool counted a whole skill YAML block as always-on cost, but only name and description are sent - over-reporting the total by 2,672 chars
findings.note: Measured across 58 live skills: 23,805 chars of frontmatter against 21,133 that can be injected. Concentrated in three third-party skills carrying licence, maintainer, website and keyword metadata: sap-abap-cds +930, sapui5 +873, sap-abap +408. The headline always-on figure drops from 32,189 to 27,237 chars - the rest of that drop is the nine deleted skills, which the old figure still counted. The tool now counts name+description and prints the difference with its three largest contributors, so the number is auditable rather than merely smaller.

findings.title: Section 5c is 840 ms - a third of the audit - and every verdict-neutral speedup available needs a new failure mode
findings.reason: Measured this round with an instrumented copy: 5c is 840 ms of a 2,481 ms run (14 node spawns at ~42 ms = 587 ms, plus ~253 ms of PowerShell-side payload and JSON work). Bounded concurrency would cut ~380 ms, but in PowerShell 5.1 it needs either one temp file pair per probe - recreating the F-068 leak class I just removed - or runspaces, whose startup cost eats the gain. Caching is F-057 and stays rejected. Accepted: a manual audit at 2.5 s, against a gate that cannot report a verdict it did not compute.

findings.title: The agent and the senior skill state four of the same rules in different words - about 2,721 chars of paraphrase against 1,758 - and both load for every ABAP development task
findings.reason: Measured: longest verbatim run between them is 60 chars, so this is paraphrase and section 3 duplication probes cannot see it. The four clusters are target confirmation, the Pre-Flight field list, preservation and test seam, and activation-is-not-correctness. Not compressed, for one reason: the skill is user-invocable and can load with no agent file present, so replacing its text with a pointer would dangle, and removing it from the agent would leave the agent silent when the skill is unavailable. Each asset must stand alone; the cost is accepted and now recorded rather than claimed absent.

findings.title: The v0.9.4.1 notes reported that 42 percent of the audit time is interpreter startup, which re-measurement does not support
findings.reason: Re-measured 2026-11-16: powershell -NoProfile -File on a trivial script is 231-240 ms across five runs, and everything outside the instrumented script span was 363-434 ms = 11-13% of wall, not 42%. The instrumented third-party measure that produced 42% counted all 21 external processes as interpreter startup, which double-counts the work each one does. The published tag cannot be rewritten without changing a released ref, so the correction lives here: interpreter startup is ~12%, and section work - 5c at 840 ms above all - is the rest.

findings.title: measure-context counted three skills as always-on cost even though each declares disable-model-invocation, over-reporting the total by 556 chars
findings.note: Measured against this session's own injected skill list: 55 of the 58 live skills appear in it, and the two that never appeared are flagged skills that were also never invoked. caveman is flagged and does appear, because the user invoked it by name - so the flagged set is now excluded from the total and named in a NOTE rather than silently subtracted. The headline always-on figure falls from 27,237 to 26,681 chars.

findings.title: measure-context printed one agent as "the main agent" with no denominator, so a per-run cost read as the cost of every run
findings.note: The folder holds 17 agent files and the tool named one of them without saying so: this session may have been running any of them, and the smallest is 6,462 chars against the printed 32,110. It now prints "agent N of M".

findings.title: Section 2 printed "skills=  0  bad_frontmatter=0  bad_links=0" for an empty skill root - a line shaped exactly like a pass
findings.note: Negative-tested: two roots that exist and hold no SKILL.md now print "ISSUE no SKILL.md under this root - nothing was checked", register an issue, and turn the run to exit 1. Before the fix the same input printed two zero lines and exited 0.

findings.title: The repo-memory/Projects duplicate scan never registered with Ran, so a run that compared nothing was indistinguishable from one that compared everything
findings.note: The block only printed on a hit. It now reports the number of files it walked under a new coverage key, so the examined-nothing verdict can see it. The run went from 20 to 21 registered sections.

findings.title: A failed git cat-file made every evidence ref resolve to "missing", producing 62 confident "no such object" findings and exit 1
findings.note: Measured with a git wrapper that exits 129 with no output: the audit printed 62 findings against 62 commits that all exist. LASTEXITCODE and the answer count are now checked first, one "cannot resolve evidence" issue is printed instead, and the per-finding check is skipped. Negative-tested: 0 "no such object" lines, 1 cannot-resolve line.

findings.title: An emptied published_skills list in removed-on-purpose.json printed a WARNING, registered nothing, and left the run clean with exit 0
findings.note: The toolkit_skills half fails loudly on an empty declaration; the published half did not, so the deletion gate could be disabled by editing its own input. Negative-tested: emptying the list now prints "the deletion gate can no longer fail" and exits 1.

findings.title: An absent MCP config printed "absent" and returned before recording coverage, so a machine with neither config reported a clean run that had verified no launcher wiring
findings.note: Negative-tested by pointing both paths at nothing: the section now also prints one WARNING that the wiring was not verified. Nothing is wrong on such a machine; what was wrong was a report implying it had been checked.

findings.title: The mirror comparison used -ne, which is case-insensitive, so a live file differing from the repository only in letter case reported identical
findings.note: Measured on 5.1.26100: "ABC" -ne "abc" is False, "ABC" -cne "abc" is True. Both the audit and install-kit now compare with -cne, and install-kit's byte comparison uses -ceq on the Base64 form for the same reason.

findings.title: Section 1 printed the raw -split line count while section 4 used Get-RealLineCount, so the same file was reported one line too long
findings.note: Measured: a 575-line agent file printed 576, and two more files printed one extra each. The phantom element comes from a trailing newline and section 4 already had the helper that removes it.

findings.title: The credential-shape rule in the audit and the one in workspace-sync.ps1 had diverged - the audit missed passwd and pwd
findings.note: Measured: a line assigning a value to passwd scored 0 hits in the audit and 1 in the writer that decides what may be mirrored. Two homes for one rule, already disagreeing. The audit's alternation now covers the same spellings.

findings.title: lesson-capture stringified an object-shaped error, so the ledger row read "[object Object]" and lost the only actionable text
findings.note: Measured: {"error":{"message":"disk full","code":28}} wrote a row reading "| error | [object Object] | 1". An object is now reduced to its .message, or serialised when there is none. Re-tested against a redirected profile: the row reads "disk full".

findings.title: lesson-capture matched a 90-character signature but stored 200 characters, so distinct failures sharing a prefix merged into one recurring failure
findings.note: The signature now spans exactly the part of the error the row keeps, so two different errors from the same statement can no longer be reported as occurrence 4 of an old one.

findings.title: lesson-capture counted matching rows rather than reading the recorded count, so rotation reset the recurrence counter and the >=3 alert could never fire again
findings.note: Rotation keeps only the last 250 rows, and the count was derived from those rows. Each row already records its own occurrence number, so the highest one is now read instead. Negative-tested with nine pre-existing rows: the next event recorded 10 and emitted the alert.

findings.title: subagent-rules decided rotation on bytes and sliced characters, so a non-ASCII log could never fall below the cap and re-rotated on every event
findings.note: Measured before the fix: a 341,090-byte Thai log rotated to 88,791 bytes and stayed above the 65,536 cap, re-reading and re-writing the whole file per event. Buffer slicing is byte-accurate. Negative-tested with a 16,390,896-byte Thai log: 30,115 bytes after one rotation and 30,178 after the next, bounded and stable, no replacement characters.

findings.title: subagent-rules rotation was an unsynchronised read-modify-write that could destroy lines appended during the window
findings.note: A rotation writes the whole file, so two interleaved rotations each discard the other's trim. The rotation now takes an exclusive-create lock, ignores a lock older than 10 s so a killed process cannot freeze it, and releases it in a finally. Verified: no lock file is left behind after a rotation.

findings.title: Every subagent-rules log write failure was swallowed, so a permanently unwritable log produced exit 0, no stderr, and a zero-byte file
findings.note: A log path pointing at a directory and a log locked with FILE_SHARE_NONE both failed silently. One stderr line is now written, and ENOENT is excluded from the stat path because a first run has no log and is not a failure - the audit's own hook probe printed false alarms until that distinction was added.

findings.title: session-drift created its state folder outside any local try, so a failure there discarded drift lines it had already computed
findings.note: The mkdir sat between buildSurface() and the diff, inside the caller's catch that returns {}. It is now guarded on its own: failing to create the folder costs the snapshot, not the report, and says so on stderr.

findings.title: install-kit reported conflicting files and still exited 0, the one outcome the script exists to report
findings.note: Measured: with one differing live agent, -Check printed "1 differ" and "DIFFERS agents\..." and exited 0, so a wrapper or a CI step read a real divergence as success. A conflict now exits 1; -Force still exits 0 because it resolved the conflict.

findings.title: sap-connection -Add warned that the secret helper did not run and exited 0, leaving the caller unable to tell whether a secret exists
findings.note: Measured with a nonexistent -SecretScript: the warning printed, the exit code was 0. It now exits 2, because the connection was written but its secret state is unknown - a partial success has to be distinguishable from a clean one.

findings.title: tooling/surface.json was a tracked runtime snapshot taken 2026-11-13, naming seven skills that removed-on-purpose.json declares deleted, and both scripts deliberately excluded it from comparison
findings.note: The file is written by the sessionStart hook on every run and by nothing else, so a tracked copy is stale by construction and uncomparable by design - it was excluded from both the installer filter and the mirror check specifically so it could not report drift. It is now untracked and removed; the live copy at ~/.copilot/state/surface.json is untouched and is what README.md:86 actually refers to.

findings.title: The senior ABAP skill told the reader to use a cheat-sheet branch that does not exist
findings.note: Measured against the GitHub API: SAP-samples/abap-cheat-sheets has exactly main, oo_patterns, rap, unit_tests, v755, v756, v757, v758, v816. There is no branch called "Standard ABAP", so an agent following the instruction would search for a name that returns nothing. The line now names the real branches.

findings.title: The RAP checkpoints stated the consequence of bypassing the BO lifecycle but not the admission test that decides whether a classic API may be called at all
findings.note: Adopted from the upstream rap skill, whose key rule is that a classic API may be used inside a RAP application only when it carries the transactional-consistent label in the Cloudification Repository. This is a process rule, not an API catalogue: it changes what the agent does before choosing an API, and it closes a gap our own text left, since a call can compile and pass ATC and still break the transactional model.

findings.title: The agent asserted that the three SAP MCP servers overlap "by roughly 85%" - a number with no measurement behind it anywhere
findings.note: The same file forbids unsourced environment claims two sections earlier. No measurement exists on this machine, so the figure is replaced by "overlap substantially", which is what the evidence supports.

findings.title: The routing table said "ADT MCP (AFF writes only)" while skills/rap-lifecycle requires the ADT scaffold generator to create CDS entities - two obligations that cannot both hold
findings.note: The "do not use" cell now exempts the scaffold generator explicitly, so the prohibition and the lifecycle agree.

findings.title: The agent authorised delegation on three conditions with no consent requirement, while both skills it tells the reader to load require the user to ask first
findings.note: Resolved in the agent's favour for the three allowlisted read-only roles, because the roster is a standing approval - and explicitly against it for everything else, including tickets and branches. Both texts now say the same thing.

findings.title: The plan/todo thresholds were decided by step count, so a one-line interface change required no plan and a three-step refactor did
findings.note: A field rename in a CDS view that four consumers read is a smaller diff than a three-step refactor and a much larger risk. Risk is now a fourth trigger, and the text says which wins when the two disagree.

findings.title: The Corrections received section carried an 828-char template that is permanently empty, costing about 210 tokens on every run of that agent
findings.note: The section is justified by its own rule and stays; only the boilerplate moved, to docs/reference/corrections.md, which is read when the first real correction arrives. The three-line pointer that remains keeps the rule visible.

findings.title: Free-text evidence was accepted silently, so a reader could not tell how much of the ledger is checkable
findings.note: Two of the 64 fixed findings cite something other than a commit, and both are legitimate - one repair's artifact lives outside this repository. They are no longer counted as verified facts with no number printed: the clean line now says "2 cite evidence that is not a commit (F-008, F-059)".

findings.title: Eight pairs of installed skills match the same realistic request, and the wrong pick costs up to 23,289 bytes - with no routing guidance anywhere in the repository
findings.note: The repository documented routing for MCP servers and nothing for skills. The pairs are owned by their installers, so editing a skill to disambiguate its trigger is overwritten by the next upgrade; a routing table in the repository survives. Added with per-pair sizes, because the sizes are what make the wrong choice expensive.

findings.title: docs/reference/environment.md documented the hook output contract but not the stdin payload each hook reads, so two hooks depended on undocumented field names
findings.note: The product documents the output shape; the input shape is unversioned. A table now records what each hook actually parses and what it does when a field is absent, and names the known weak point: a hook cannot enumerate the harness payload, so a new field name has to be added by hand.

findings.title: F-074 accepted section 5c as unfixable on an incomplete premise, then the fix was built and measured to be 51% slower than leaving it alone
findings.reason: The round-3 reason named two options - one temp file per probe, or runspaces - and concluded both were bad. A third existed and was not considered: .NET Process with redirected streams and no temp file. It was built this round. In isolation it was 3.5x faster (2,435 to 697 ms for 14 probes); inside the audit it made the whole run slower, 2,070 to 3,119 ms median over three interleaved pairs. The isolated win came from a near-empty probe home; in the audit each child reads the roster and fourteen concurrent starts contend for one disk. Reverted, and the reason is now recorded at the code so nobody rebuilds it. The round-3 reasoning was incomplete; its conclusion was right.
findings.note: Accepted on purpose. See reason.

findings.title: Section 5c remains about a third of the audit, and the only measured alternative was slower
findings.reason: Re-measured this round on a quiet machine: 873-1,003 ms of a 2,472-2,824 ms run, unchanged in share from the 840 ms measured in round 2. The audit grew by about 250-350 ms overall this round because it now performs more checks - the empty-root guard, the coverage registration, the evidence-failure path - and that is the trade a gate should make. Accepted.
findings.note: Accepted on purpose. See reason.

findings.title: SETUP-NEW-MACHINE.md has been checked line by line against the repository but has never been executed on a machine that did not already have the toolkit
findings.reason: Every command in it was verified this round against the files it names, and seven command-level errors were fixed in round 3. That is a review, not a run. A single dry run on a fresh Windows profile is the only remaining proof, and it cannot be produced from inside the machine being described. Disclosed rather than claimed.
findings.note: Accepted on purpose. See reason.

findings.title: Three .bak copies of the se38 skill body sit inside a live skill folder, 27,628 bytes in total
findings.reason: Measured: SKILL.md.bak-20261101-compact 10,836 B, .bak-20261101-tools 8,396 B, .bak-20261101-tools2 8,396 B. They cost no context - the loader reads SKILL.md only - and they are the way back to a previous body. The owner's call, reported rather than taken.
findings.note: Accepted on purpose. See reason.

findings.title: A 919-char paragraph appears in 15 toolkit files and a 526-char paragraph in 28, but the cost is per-run, not always-on
findings.reason: Measured: 15 and 28 copies in the toolkit-owned loader roots. Both paragraphs sit in agent and skill bodies, which load only when that agent or skill runs; the always-on budget is name+description and is unaffected. Removing them would mean editing files the next npx skills or toolkit upgrade overwrites, for a saving that materialises only during those runs. Left to the packages that own them.
findings.note: Accepted on purpose. See reason.

findings.title: A lock-tracked skill refers to two skills that exist in no loader root
findings.note: Accepted on purpose. See reason.
findings.reason: Measured: ultracave and megacave are absent from all 69 skill folders across the three loader roots. The line is "/caveman ultra and /caveman wenyan are aliases: follow the ultracave or megacave skill instead of this one", so the aliases point at nothing and a reader asking for ultra is told to load a skill that cannot load. Not fixed here because .skill-lock.json records the skill as coming from JuliusBrussee/caveman: an edit is overwritten by the next npx skills update, so it belongs upstream. Reported rather than silently patched. The routing doc now states the flat-name convention that causes the neighbouring case.

findings.title: Ten sibling-skill references name a .md file that does not exist because the installer flattens files into folders
findings.note: Accepted on purpose. See reason.
findings.reason: Measured: 10 backticked <name>.md mentions across 3 skills resolve to a sibling skill folder and to no file - convert-ui5-to-fiori-elements 8, modernize-ui5-app 1, migrate-segw-to-rap 1, naming 4 distinct skills. Upstream these are flat files in one directory, so the text is correct in its own repository and stale only as installed. All three are lock-tracked from arc-mcp/arc-1, so an edit is lost on update. Recorded in docs/tool-routing.md instead, which is where an agent looks after loading one of them.

findings.title: create-arc1-extension points at ../../../docs_page/extensions.md, which resolves outside every loader root and does not exist
findings.note: Accepted on purpose. See reason.
findings.reason: Measured: the relative path resolves to C:\Users\narue\.agents\docs_page\extensions.md and C:\Users\narue\docs_page does not exist either. Three lines point at it, including one labelled "point the developer here", so the named documentation is unreachable from the machine that installed the skill. Lock-tracked from arc-mcp/arc-1: an edit is overwritten by the next update, so this is reported for upstream rather than patched locally.

findings.title: sap-abap-cds is GPL-3.0 while every other installed skill is unlicensed or permissive - a licence the owner has not reviewed
findings.note: Accepted on purpose. See reason.
findings.reason: Measured: the only GPL-3.0 skill across 69, with maintainer metadata pointing at sap-ai-skills.com. It is also the one skill with a references folder that is not lock-tracked, so it is the editable copy. Whether a copyleft licence is acceptable for text that is loaded into a closed internal assistant is a decision for the owner, not a defect this audit can fix - and deleting or relicensing a third-party file would be worse than surfacing it. Flagged once, deliberately without a recommendation.

findings.title: docs/tool-routing.md quoted the modernize-ui5-app character count in a column of byte counts
findings.note: Measured: modernize-ui5-app is 80,252 bytes / 79,726 chars, so the row quoted chars while every other row quoted bytes - 12 of 13 figures in that column were exact, which is what made the odd one hard to see. Corrected to 80,252.

findings.title: docs/tool-routing.md claimed the two debugging descriptions share a 293-character sentence; the shared run is 314 characters and the shorter description is 78 percent duplicated
findings.note: Measured on the frontmatter description only: abap-debugging is 404 chars, abap-runtime-analysis 447, longest common run 314, and 314 of 404 chars of the shorter one fall inside shared runs of 20+ chars. The row now states the duplication ratio, which is the figure that justifies the routing decision.

findings.title: Ran memory.dup had a hard floor of 1, so the coverage registration added in round 3 could never report zero - the state it exists to expose
findings.note: Measured: [Math]::Max(1, count) always registers at least one comparison. Negative-tested by forcing the count to 0: the run now reaches the examined-nothing path instead of counting a comparison that never happened.

findings.title: The launcher check incremented the verified counter directly instead of registering with Ran, so it inflated the clean count and stayed invisible to the examined-nothing verdict
findings.note: Measured before the fix: 505 items reported against a ran-sum of 503, the difference being exactly the two Test-LauncherWiring call sites. After: launcher registers 2 and the clean line reports 22 sections instead of 21.

findings.title: The skill frontmatter check tested for the substring name: anywhere in the file, so a skill whose frontmatter name differs from its folder passed
findings.note: Borrowed from the upstream validator (likweitan/abap-skills, scripts/validate_skills.py: if name != skill_file.parent.name), which checks four SKILL.md-local invariants we did not. Negative-tested: a folder wrong-folder holding name: some-other-name now prints BAD with both values and exits 1, while a correctly named sibling is not flagged.

findings.title: Three stale measured numbers in code comments contradicted the scripts own output
findings.note: Measured: the commit-history scan costs 224-238 ms, not the tenth of a second the comment claimed; section 5c is about a quarter of the run, not the 55% it claimed after the audit grew; the ledger comment said 2 of 64 findings cite non-commit evidence while the line below it printed 4 of 115; and measure-context restated a 23,805/2,672 pair that its own run had already changed. Each now states the rule, or points at the line that prints the current number.

findings.title: The main agent file was 32,828 bytes, of which about 1,200 were narrative that could not change a decision
findings.note: Measured: 32,828 -> 31,623 bytes, -1,205. Every cut was a history note, a motivation clause, or a restated obligation; 31 obligation probes over the touched sections all still match and all 24 section headings remain. A density pass over the remaining 31 KB found 90% of it is already pointer-dense tables and one-line rules, so the lossless ceiling was about 10% and this took the available 4%.

findings.title: A 917-character Workspace preflight paragraph is duplicated in 15 files across 8 distinct variants, 14,073 characters in total
findings.note: Accepted on purpose. See reason.
findings.reason: Measured: 15 copies, 8 variants, largest group 6 byte-identical files. Every copy sits inside an agent or skill body, which loads only when that agent or skill runs - none of it is in the always-on budget, which is name+description and was re-measured this round at 26,681 chars. The files belong to sap-ai-dev-toolkit, whose installer overwrites edits on upgrade, so a local fix is lost work; the right home is upstream. Recorded rather than patched.

findings.title: Three -by-pongg agents declare a skill the toolkit also installs, and each restates the skill gate, so one job costs up to 25,183 bytes
findings.note: Accepted on purpose. See reason.
findings.reason: Measured: se38 agent 6,929 + skill 15,427 = 22,356 B; st22 agent 9,630 + skill 15,553 = 25,183 B. The composition is deliberate - the agent is a router and the skill is the procedure, and the agent declares it with skills: so the loader composes them. Cutting the gate from the agent would leave it silent if the skill is unavailable, which is the same argument F-075 recorded for the senior skill. Both files are user-owned, so the trade is the owner to make; reported with the number rather than changed.

findings.title: A user-invocable skill that is also disable-model-invocation was believed to be a contradiction; no installed skill has both keys true
findings.note: Accepted on purpose. See reason.
findings.reason: Measured across the three loader roots: exactly three skills carry disable-model-invocation: true (caveman, grill-with-docs, improve-codebase-architecture) and none of them declares user-invocable at all; the two SAP skills that DO declare user-invocable: true declare disable-model-invocation: false or omit the key, so they are model-invocable by declaration, not by a loader bug. The pairing the earlier round suspected exists in zero files, so there is nothing to repair. Recorded so the belief is not re-investigated.
